approach: Add one reading-acceptance check, `check_scope_limit` in crates/athena-core/src/reading/checks.rs, as a single `step!(check_scope_limit(reading));` line in `refusing_check` after `check_defined_terms` and before `check_boundary_and_repo_files`. Root cause: nothing at the reading gate compares a scope limit with the files Athena always writes (CHANGELOG.md, forced by `ensure_changelog`, reading.rs:297, run before the gate at reading.rs:859) or with the readers of a changed config. A limit written from the named files therefore passes the gate and fails at verification (class scope-criterion-too-narrow-misses-dependent-tests; jobs 20261018-045437-7z81 and 20261023-052543-9bw7). Round-5 change (finding 4): the matcher and the parse of the limit's allowed-file words now live in ONE function in briefs.rs, `change_limit(text) -> Option<ChangeLimit>`, which `limits_changed_files` (briefs.rs:146) becomes a one-line wrapper over (`change_limit(text).is_some()`). The gate uses that function, so it cannot read a sentence differently from the matcher that builds the allowlist at verification (`allowed_paths`, briefs.rs:115). `ChangeLimit` has `bare` (true for 'no other file changed' and 'production unchanged', which name no allowed list) and `allowed` (the matcher's own word list: the words between `only` and `may` for 'only X may change', the words between `outside` and the change word for 'no file outside X changed', all words for 'test-only change'). The gate takes the first limiting criterion in reading order, the same one `limiting_criterion` (briefs.rs:103) enforces. Checks, for capability `change` readings with no question, no repo scan: (1) CHANGELOG half: a non-bare limit is accepted when its `allowed` words contain `changelog.md` (from the default-written table) or the two words `the deliverables`; otherwise refused. A CHANGELOG.md deliverable alone does not repair the text, because `ensure_changelog` lists it at the gate in production. (2) Config half: when a limit exists (bare or not) and athena.toml or defaults.toml is a deliverable, the reading needs a `Consumers:` assumption whose path-like words (config files themselves ignored) are ALL deliverables (or under a deliverable ending in '/'), and which either names at least one such path or says 'none found', 'unchanged' or 'no change'. A named path that is not a deliverable is refused whatever else the line says (finding 5). Round-5 scope changes: steward.rs is no longer touched (finding 2); the queue effect is shown through `check_reading_text`, the function `queued_work` calls, in a reading.rs test. run/tests.rs stays as one forced constant edit (finding 1). The share of past readings newly refused is measured by the verification replay, not by the producer (finding 6).

decisions.choice: One matcher: add `change_limit(text) -> Option<ChangeLimit>` in briefs.rs next to `limits_changed_files`, make `limits_changed_files` return `change_limit(text).is_some()`, and have the gate read `ChangeLimit.allowed` and `.bare`. checks.rs holds no sentence parser of its own, only a lowercase-word comparison against the table rows.
decisions.reason: Finding 4: the earlier `limit_span` started at the first trigger word anywhere and used triggers (except, beyond, besides) the matcher never uses, so 'No other file is changed beyond formatting' (matched as a bare form) was refused, and an earlier unmatched 'only' before 'no file outside crates/ and CHANGELOG.md changed' opened the wrong span. Returning the allowed words from the clause that actually matched removes both, and the gate and verification cannot drift. The refactor keeps the loop and its windows (OUTSIDE_WINDOW, CHANGED_WINDOW, ONLY_WINDOW, TEST_ONLY_WINDOW, OTHER_FILE_WINDOW) and the first-match-in-word-order result, so `limits_changed_files` gives the same answers; the existing briefs.rs and run_pin_tests.rs matcher tests are the guard, and a new briefs test pins the allowed words for each form.

rejected.option: Keep `limit_span` in checks.rs and only drop except/beyond/besides
rejected.why: Still a second sentence parser that starts at the first trigger word anywhere, not at the matched clause; the finding's own second example would still be refused.

rejected.option: Free negation-word window around the name (rounds 2 and 3)
rejected.why: 'keeping', 'kept', 'stays' have positive uses; the matched clause's allowed list needs no word list.

rejected.option: Accept when CHANGELOG.md is a deliverable (the literal reading of criterion 2)
rejected.why: Inert for production readings: `ensure_changelog` (reading.rs:859) lists it before the gate, so the class would stay open. Criterion 2's 'listed' is shown as 'named in the limit's allowed list'.

rejected.option: Make `ensure_changelog` append CHANGELOG.md to the limit text
rejected.why: Rewrites the reader's criterion silently, so the reader never learns the rule, and the config half would still need a refusal.

decisions.choice: Bare forms ('No other file is changed', 'production unchanged') are exempt from the CHANGELOG half. 'Test-only change' carries all its words as `allowed`, so it is accepted only when it also names CHANGELOG.md or 'the deliverables'. Known misses go in D166: a bare form that in fact forbids CHANGELOG.md, a negation inside the allowed list, and a second limiting criterion after the first (verification also reads only the first).
decisions.reason: A bare form names no allowed list, so there is nothing to compare; flagging it would refuse every 'No other file is changed' reading, including the defaults-proposal job. Test-only jobs still must edit CHANGELOG.md, so they are held to the rule.

rejected.option: Refuse bare forms too
rejected.why: Would refuse a large share of readings with no way to repair beyond rewording the sentence; the higher refusal rate is intended only for lists that omit the file.

rejected.option: Fire only when the limit names a file (round 1)
rejected.why: Leaves 'test-only change' accepted although the job must edit CHANGELOG.md.

decisions.choice: Only criteria are scanned, through the first limiting criterion (as `limiting_criterion`); out_of_scope items are not.
decisions.reason: Verification reads criteria only (briefs.rs:103-108); out_of_scope items are exclusions, and 'files kept from job X' would cause false refusals. This departs from the reading's 'criterion or out_of_scope item'; raised as a User question.

rejected.option: Also scan out_of_scope items
rejected.why: Enforcement ignores them; false refusals.

decisions.choice: Consumers line rule (finding 5): every path-like word on the line, other than athena.toml and defaults.toml, must be a deliverable path or under a deliverable ending in '/'. A line is valid when it has at least one such path, or says 'none found', 'unchanged' or 'no change'. A non-deliverable path makes the line invalid even if the line says 'unchanged'. Path-like = contains '/' or ends .rs/.toml/.md/.json/.yml/.yaml after trimming quotes, backticks, brackets, a leading './' and end punctuation.
decisions.reason: With a limit the deliverable list is the allowlist (briefs.rs:110-126). In 7z81 the tests that loaded the real athena.toml were not deliverables, so the scope guard failed the job. 'Consumers: crates/athena-cli/tests/common/mod.rs must be updated; others unchanged' would still be that shape, so a named non-deliverable is refused. A consumer that needs no change is simply left off the line, or the line says 'none found'. athena.toml is also read outside crates/ (xtask/tests/policy.rs, xtask/src/main.rs), so every path-like word counts. The defaults-proposal job (`accept_request`, proposals.rs:442-450, via `ask` at proposals.rs:642) lists defaults.toml and its reader will write 'No other file is changed', so it needs one `Consumers:` line, `Consumers: none found` being accepted; the refusal text names the exact line and is the re-read feedback (reading.rs:688).

rejected.option: Accept form (b) whenever 'unchanged' appears (round 4)
rejected.why: Finding 5: passes the 7z81 shape.

rejected.option: Accept a non-deliverable path only when the line says that path is unchanged
rejected.why: Needs a clause parser between the path and the word; leaving the path off the line gives the same result with no parsing.

rejected.option: Accept any crates/ test deliverable as the answer (literal criterion 3)
rejected.why: An unrelated test deliverable satisfies it with no search and no widening of the allowlist to the real consumers.

rejected.option: Exempt bare limits on proposal-apply jobs
rejected.why: A defaults change has the 7z81 risk; an exemption keyed to the request text is a hole.

rejected.option: Scan repo contents for files that load the config
rejected.why: Out of scope; readers see a plain copy and the gate must stay deterministic.

decisions.choice: Measurement of the refusal share is the verification replay's job (finding 6). The producer does no measurement; it reports in its output that the share is measured at verification (`replay_is_held`, replay.rs:296; limit `replay_limit_percent` 304; declared 3% + REPLAY_DECLARED_MARGIN_POINTS 5 = 8%, replay.rs:161) because the producer snapshot has no records/ or history. If the verification replay measures more than 8%, the instruction to whoever reads the result is to report the measured share and not to narrow the check or edit the declared figure.
decisions.reason: System facts: the producer snapshot has no records/ and no history, so no stored readings or replay result exist there. The 3% figure is an estimate, not measured.

risks.risk: Refactoring `limits_changed_files` into `change_limit` changes what it matches and so changes verification-time enforcement.
risks.mitigation: The loop, windows, match order and returns stay the same; the function only also returns the matched clause's words. Existing matcher tests in briefs.rs and run_pin_tests.rs:1353-1396 stay unchanged and must pass, and the new test asserts `limits_changed_files(t) == change_limit(t).is_some()` over the phrases they use.

risks.risk: False refusals: a limit that is only mentioned in passing is matched and its allowed list omits CHANGELOG.md.
risks.mitigation: The matcher already errs toward not matching (briefs.rs:140-145). The repair is one phrase ('and CHANGELOG.md' in the list, or 'the deliverables'), given in the error text. Bare forms stay accepted and are pinned by corpus Accept cases. The verification replay holds the change if the newly refused share exceeds 8%.

risks.risk: The Consumers rule cannot verify that a search was done; 'none found' can be written without searching, and a consumer the reader does not name is not caught.
risks.mitigation: D166 states the limit: the gate forces the question and checks that every named consumer is a deliverable; scanning repo content is out of scope.

risks.risk: Known misses of the allowed-list rule: a bare form that really forbids CHANGELOG.md, a negation inside the allowed list, and a second limiting criterion after the first.
risks.mitigation: Named in D166. The first-criterion choice mirrors enforcement (`limiting_criterion`), so a miss at the gate is also not enforced at verification.

risks.risk: A defaults-proposal job fails reading twice and stalls.
risks.mitigation: The refusal text names the exact line to add (`Consumers: none found`, `... unchanged`, or deliverable paths) and the new READING_RULES line says the same; the refusal text is the re-read feedback (reading.rs:688). Unit and corpus cases pin refuse-then-accept for the accept_request shape. A second failure goes through the unchanged ReadError::Refused path.

risks.risk: The new READING_RULES line pushes a rule line past 220 bytes or the section past its bound.
risks.mitigation: Keep the line to about 200 bytes; if the section exceeds the bound, set the bound to the measured size plus a small margin and fix its comment. `cargo test -p athena-context` shows it. The reader prompt is untouched.

risks.risk: Another test or fake reader outside the places found pushes a limit phrase through the gate and starts failing.
risks.mitigation: Step 10 runs `cargo test --locked` for the whole workspace. A failing fixture gets 'and CHANGELOG.md' in its limit text, as LIMIT does; the check is not weakened.

risks.risk: run/tests.rs is outside the six listed deliverables, so a scope guard built from the job's deliverable list could flag it.
risks.mitigation: The edit is one constant and its comment, listed in `files`, explained in the CHANGELOG entry and D166, raised as a User question and checked by `git diff --stat`. steward.rs, the other extra file of round 4, is dropped.

risks.risk: A Consumers line with a `./` prefix, quotes or backticks, or a prose word, is mis-parsed and refused.
risks.mitigation: Trim quotes, backticks, brackets, './' and end punctuation as `allowed_paths` does (briefs.rs:119-120); a deliverable ending in '/' covers paths under it; unit and corpus cases pin both forms. A word like 'e.g.' is not path-like (no '/', no listed extension).

risks.risk: The replay share exceeds 8% at verification and holds the job.
risks.mitigation: The producer reports in its output that the share is measured at verification and does not narrow the check or edit the declared figure; the measured share goes to the user, who decides.
